content: Do not take irbesartan and hydrochlorothiazide if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as it may harm the fetus. The combination of irbesartan and hydrochlorothiazide is prescribed to treat high blood pressure. Irbesartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin II receptor antagonists, which work by blocking the action of certain natural chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, or water pill, that helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. This medication is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Irbesartan and hydrochlorothiazide help control high blood pressure but do not cure it. It may take 2 to 4 weeks to experience the full benefits. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before taking irbesartan and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to irbesartan, hydrochlorothiazide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention aspirin, NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), cholestyramine, colestipol, lithium, diabetes medications, narcotic pain relievers, oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, prednisone), other blood pressure medications, phenobarbital, and tolbutamide. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are on dialysis or have a history of asthma, lupus, diabetes, heart failure, gout, or kidney or liver disease. Let your doctor know if you are breastfeeding. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can worsen the side effects of this medication. Irbesartan and hydrochlorothiazide may cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, especially when standing up quickly. To minimize this, rise slowly from a lying position and rest your feet on the floor before standing. Dehydration from diarrhea, vomiting, insufficient fluid intake, or excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet or an exercise program, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Common side effects of irbesartan and hydrochlorothiazide include dizziness, extreme tiredness, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, heartburn, chest pain, and flu-like symptoms. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include dry mouth, thirst, weakness, lack of energy, restlessness, confusion, seizures, muscle pain or cramps, infrequent urination, rapid heartbeat, lightheadedness, or fainting. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may order tests to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
